config.title: Generic List<T>

intro.title: Generic List<T>
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable list component that can display any type of data, such as a list of names, numbers, or custom objects. You will learn how to use TypeScript generics, specifically the Generic List<T> pattern, to create flexible and type-safe components in React. The main technologies involved are React functional components, JSX for rendering, and TypeScript's generic type parameters. By the end, you will understand how to write a single component that works with multiple data types while ensuring your code is robust and easy to maintain.
intro.usecase: Generic List<T> patterns appear in nearly every React application that displays dynamic data collections. You'll use them when building product catalogs with filterable item grids, user dashboards with sortable data tables, or social media feeds that render different post types. This approach allows developers to create reusable components that can display any type of data while maintaining type safety and reducing code duplication. For example, a single <GenericList> component could render employee directories, project task lists, or e-commerce product cards without rewriting display logic for each data type.

objectives: Implement a generic List<T> component that accepts a type parameter for its items.
Initialize and manage state for a list of items using the useState hook.
Construct a handler function to add new items of a specified type to the list.
Render the list items dynamically by mapping over the state array.
Apply type safety by defining and using an interface for the item structure.
Configure the component to display a message when the list is empty.
Integrate user input controls to manipulate the list contents.

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React APIs are imported, enabling you to create components with state.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statement. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main GenericList component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named GenericList that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function with the name GenericList and have it return null.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the GenericList component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A GenericList component is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: The component is named GenericList and returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the GenericList component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly GenericList and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've defined a component named GenericList that returns null.

steps.title: Add props parameter to GenericList
steps.instruction: Add a props parameter to the GenericList component that includes 'items' and 'renderItem' properties.
steps.hint: The props parameter should be an object with two properties: items (an array) and renderItem (a function).
steps.expectedOutcome: The GenericList component now accepts props containing items and renderItem.
successCriteria: GenericList has a props parameter defined in its function signature.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a props parameter to the GenericList function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The props parameter is missing. Add (props) after GenericList to define the component's interface.

steps.title: Initialize state for the list items
steps.instruction: Inside the GenericList component, use the useState hook to create a state variable called 'items' and initialize it with the 'items' property from props.
steps.hint: Call useState with props.items as the initial value and destructure the returned array into a state variable and setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'items' initialized with the items passed via props, ready to be displayed and updated.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with props.items as initial value, and the returned array is destructured into 'items' and 'setItems'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're calling useState with props.items and destructuring the result into [items, setItems].
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're using the useState hook correctly. You need to call useState(props.items) and destructure the result into a state variable and setter function.

steps.title: Create a function to add new items
steps.instruction: Inside the GenericList component, create a function named addItem that takes a parameter (newItem) and updates the state by adding that new item to the existing items array.
steps.hint: Use the setItems function from useState to update the state. You can use the spread operator to create a new array with the existing items plus the new item.
steps.expectedOutcome: The addItem function should be defined inside the component and update the state correctly.
successCriteria: The addItem function is defined, takes a parameter, and uses setItems with the spread operator to add the new item.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your addItem function properly updates the state using setItems and the spread operator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addItem function is missing or doesn't correctly update the state. Remember to use setItems to add the new item to the existing array.

steps.title: Create a function to remove items
steps.instruction: Inside your GenericList component, create a function named removeItem that takes an index parameter and updates the items state by removing the item at that index.
steps.hint: You can use the setItems function with a callback that filters the current items array based on the index.
steps.expectedOutcome: The removeItem function is defined inside the component and uses setItems to update the state by removing an item at the given index.
successCriteria: A removeItem function is created that takes an index parameter and updates the items state correctly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the removeItem function might not be updating the state correctly. Make sure it uses setItems to filter out the item at the given index.
steps.feedbackWrong: The removeItem function is missing or doesn't update the state properly. Try creating a function that takes an index and uses setItems with a filter to remove that item.

steps.title: Return the basic JSX structure
steps.instruction: In your GenericList component, return a div container from the component.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a JSX div element. The div can be empty for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a JSX div element instead of null.
successCriteria: The component returns a JSX div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning a JSX div element from the component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a JSX div element. Check your return statement.

steps.title: Render the list items using the renderItem prop
steps.instruction: Inside your component, map over the items state array and call the renderItem prop for each item. Return the result inside the div.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the items array. For each item, call props.renderItem(item) and return it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will be able to display each item using the renderItem function passed as a prop.
successCriteria: The items array is mapped, and props.renderItem is called for each item inside the div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling props.renderItem for each item and returning the result inside the div.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try mapping over the items array and calling props.renderItem(item) for each element.

steps.title: Add an input and button for adding items
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add an input field and a button before the existing div. The button's onClick should call the addItem function with the input's current value.
steps.hint: Use JSX to add an <input> element and a <button> element. Remember to connect the button's onClick handler to call addItem.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have UI controls (input and button) that allow users to add new items to the list.
successCriteria: An input field and a button are added inside the return statement. The button's onClick handler calls addItem.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some elements, but make sure both the input and button are present and the button has an onClick handler that calls addItem.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UI controls for adding items are missing or incomplete. Add an input field and a button with an onClick handler that calls addItem.

steps.title: Add remove buttons for each list item
steps.instruction: Inside your map function, add a remove button next to each rendered item and wire its onClick to call removeItem with the item's index.
steps.hint: Add a button element with an onClick handler that calls removeItem(index). Place it after the rendered item content.
steps.analogousExample:

{item}
))
steps.expectedOutcome: Each list item will have a remove button that, when clicked, removes that specific item from the list.
successCriteria: A remove button is added next to each rendered item with an onClick handler that calls removeItem with the item's index.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it's inside the map function and calls removeItem with the correct index.
steps.feedbackWrong: The remove button isn't properly implemented. Check that you're adding it inside the map function and wiring the onClick handler correctly.
